messages:
Aisha (support): Hi team — customer ACME reported a sudden jump in p95 for streaming responses starting ~2026-03-12. They say non-streaming calls unchanged. Uploading repro and logs from the tenant.
Jon (support-engineer): thanks — do we have a tenant id / sample request? any client-side changes? "+customer says they didn't change anything on their side".
Aisha (support): Tenant: acme-corp-42. Example request: a short chat with streaming=true, prompt ~80 tokens. Baseline p95 used to be ~220ms; reported p95 is ~680ms, p99 ~1.6s. Total time for sync non-stream call is ~480ms, so streaming TTFB is what they complain about — first chunk arriving later than before.
maria (customer-rep): they attached a curl repro against hosted endpoint (api.redwood.ai/v1/chat). They also observed that sometimes the first chunk is immediate but subsequent chunks come in bursts.
Priya (eng-runtime): interesting — that pattern sounds like chunk coalescing/flush drift, not pure model latency. Was there any change to flush heuristics, kernel timers, or a new batching tweak rolled this week?
Marco (infra): we did push a kernel-level change to reduce syscalls in chunk writer on 2026-03-11 (deploy id: canary-2026-03-11b). It changed the writer to wait up to 6ms to aggregate tiny writes before flush. The intent was to reduce network IO for tiny tokens.
Jon (support-engineer): can that increase TTFB for the first chunk? Customer says sometimes first chunk delayed but sometimes it's fine — so probabilistic.
Priya (eng-runtime): yes — if the runtime's first-chunk heuristic was relying on immediate post-token flush and the kernel change introduced a small aggregation window, p95 could shift upward. But why non-stream total time not similarly affected? Because sync path buffers until final content, so small aggregation helps with throughput but hurts streaming TTFB.
Aisha (support): we should reproduce internally. Repro steps from customer: 
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -d '{"model":"rwd-small-3","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"short question"}]}'
```
They say toggling streaming=false keeps p95 low.
Marco (infra): I'll spin up a canary with the previous kernel writer behavior (no aggregation) and run a head-to-head.
Priya (eng-runtime): also want to check flush_interval and chunk size heuristics in runtime config. There are two knobs: streaming.min_flush_ms and streaming.max_aggregation_bytes. If min_flush_ms was implicitly affected by kernel-level coalescing, effective flush could be up to 6-8ms for small outputs.
Jon (support-engineer): customer logs show first-chunk latency histogram with a sharp mode at ~35ms previously; now it's got a shoulder at ~200-800ms. That's p95 impact.
maria (customer-rep): they flagged it's a regression — they noticed after a platform update on 2026-03-11. They want a mitigation ASAP; threatened to fallback to another provider for edge interactive flows.
Priya (eng-runtime): immediate mitigation options:
- rollback kernel writer change (infra action)
- adjust runtime to force immediate flush for first N tokens (cheap patch)
- provide tenant workaround by adding a query param `streaming_hint=low_latency` to disable aggregation on a per-tenant basis
We can do (2) quickly.
Marco (infra): rolling back is possible but would need a canary and verification. I can revert the change in the canary cluster now. If it matches baseline metrics, we can schedule rollback.
Aisha (support): can we ask customer to toggle a header for now? any ad-hoc header we support? e.g., `X-Streaming-Mode: eager`?
Priya (eng-runtime): we don't currently parse that header. But we can enable a runtime flag `force_first_chunk_flush=true` per deployment and patch config for the tenant route. That change is a runtime config flip, deploy-safe.
Jon (support-engineer): I'll prepare a patch to perform immediate flush for the first N tokens (N=1) and deploy to canary.
deploy-bot: Starting canary deploy rwd-runtime@2026-03-12-09:14 (force-first-chunk-flush)
Priya (eng-runtime): patch is small; pseudocode:
```
if (streaming && token_count <= 1) {
  flushImmediately(); // bypass aggregation window
}
```
We'll also add telemetry tag `streaming_first_chunk_ms` to compare.
Marco (infra): canary revert test running now between two sets: writer-agg (current prod) vs writer-noagg (pre-change) vs runtime-first-flush (patch). I'll run synthetic load simulating ACME's prompt distribution.
Aisha (support): ACME on standby for canary test. Maria — can you ask them for a test key to route to canary edge?
maria (customer-rep): sent test key, they can hit canary endpoint. They asked if there's an interim workaround: they can set streaming=false but that increases total latency and UX is worse.
Priya (eng-runtime): initial canary data: writer-noagg brings p95 back to ~240ms, runtime-first-flush reduces p95 to ~260ms. Writer-noagg is slightly better but runtime patch is almost immediate mitigation.
Jon (support-engineer): recommend we roll runtime-first-flush to all customers as a hotfix, and schedule infra rollback vs a more nuanced aggregation rule. We'll also document the tradeoff: more small writes -> increased network packets and slightly higher p50 throughput cost.
Marco (infra): agreed. We should also add a telemetry flag to detect tenants that rely on low-latency streaming and mark for SLA/opt-in.
Aisha (support): messaging to customer: apologize, explain root cause (kernel-level aggregation interaction with runtime flush heuristics), mitigation rolled within hours (force-first-chunk flush), and longer-term fix: either revert aggregation or implement smarter heuristics (only aggregate when token emission rate < threshold). Ask if they want the fix enabled for their tenant now.
maria (customer-rep): customer accepted the hotfix and confirmed p95 improved on canary to ~250ms. They asked for a written postmortem and for us to whitelist them for low-latency route until we finalize.
Priya (eng-runtime): follow-ups: 
- PR to add `force_first_chunk_flush` config + tests (done)
- infra follow-up to evaluate rollback vs adaptive aggregation (Marco)
- add e2e tests simulating gRPC/HTTP chunk coalescing and client flush patterns
- doc update: streaming best-practices + headers/workarounds
Jon (support-engineer): also adding an alert rule: if streaming p95 increases >2x baseline AND sync path p95 stable, create an SCC incident. That should catch aggregation regressions specifically.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy complete. rwd-runtime@2026-03-12-09:27 (force-first-chunk-flush) -> success
Aisha (support): great. Closing loop: customer is happy for now, will monitor next 48h. I'll draft the PM and postmortem template.
Priya (eng-runtime): note for longer term: consider per-tenant adaptive strategy and expose `streaming_mode=eager|balanced|throughput` in API so clients can choose.
Marco (infra): will schedule infra review for the kernel writer change and identify safer aggregation thresholds. Also add a perf benchmark to PRs touching writer.
Jon (support-engineer): adding reproduction scripts to internal support repo under support/diagnostics/streaming-first-chunk to speed future triage.
Aisha (support): thanks everyone. Marking thread resolved but keep monitoring. :thumbsup:
